author: PushEngage
description: PushEngage Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Lets AI assistants like Claude Desktop and Cursor authenticate against PushEngage and send push notifications on your behalf.
name: PushEngage MCP

tools.description: Opens a browser window to the PushEngage dashboard. After you click Authorize, an access token is stored locally and used for subsequent calls; the expiry is shown in the result. Requires a browser on the local machine. In headless or SSH environments the authorization URL is printed to the terminal so it can be opened manually.
tools.name: pushengage_auth_login
tools.title: Log in to PushEngage

tools.description: Returns the current login state: authenticated (bool), expires_at (token expiry ISO string), current_site_id, api_url, dashboard_url, and client_name. Use this to check whether pushengage_auth_login is needed before making other calls.
tools.name: pushengage_auth_status
tools.title: Check authentication and site status

tools.description: Revokes the current PushEngage session on the server and deletes the locally stored token. After this call, all site-scoped tools require pushengage_auth_login before they can be used again.
tools.name: pushengage_auth_logout
tools.title: Log out

tools.description: Lists PushEngage sites the authenticated user can access. Returns site_id, site_name, site_url, and site_status. Also returns current_site_id so the assistant can see which site is already active without calling pushengage_auth_status. When the user asks to send a notification linking to their site's homepage, use site_url as the notification's url field.
tools.name: pushengage_list_sites
tools.title: List sites

tools.description: Sets the current site used by all site-scoped tools (pushengage_send_notification, pushengage_list_segments, pushengage_get_analytics_summary, pushengage_list_drip_campaigns, etc.) when no site_id is provided. Persists across MCP restarts. Call pushengage_list_sites first to get a valid site_id.
tools.name: pushengage_select_site
tools.title: Select current site

tools.description: Returns the current site's details, matching the dashboard's Site Details page: name, URL, image, timezone, geolocation toggle, and the "Powered By PushEngage" branding toggle.
tools.name: pushengage_get_site_details
tools.title: Get site details

tools.description: Updates the current site's details. Pass only the fields you want to change: site_name (Site Name), site_url (Site URL), timezone (Website Time Zone, an IANA name), enable_geolocation (Enable Geolocation), and/or remove_powered_by_pushengage (Remove "Powered By PushEngage", which needs a paid plan). Provide at least one field. Returns the updated site details.

site_url.description: Site URL. A full http(s) URL, e.g. https://example.com.

timezone.description: Website Time Zone as an IANA name, e.g. "America/New_York" or "Asia/Kolkata".

enable_geolocation.description: Enable Geolocation. Personalizes notifications based on the subscriber's location and timezone.

remove_powered_by_pushengage.description: Remove "Powered By PushEngage" branding from notifications. Requires a paid (white-label) plan; the API rejects it otherwise.

tools.name: pushengage_update_site_details
tools.title: Update site details

tools.description: Returns the current site's campaign default settings: utm_parameters (enabled + source/medium/campaign/term/content), fallback_notification (title/message/url), fallback_attributes (city/country), and default_expiry (broken into total_seconds + days/hours/minutes). These are the defaults applied to push campaigns, matching the dashboard's Campaign Defaults page.
tools.name: pushengage_get_campaign_defaults
tools.title: Get campaign defaults

tools.description: Updates one or more of the current site's campaign default settings. Pass only the groups and fields you want to change: utm_parameters, fallback_notification, fallback_attributes, and/or default_expiry. The tool reads the current values and merges your changes, so partial edits are fine (e.g. change just utm_parameters.source, or set default_expiry to {days:7}). default_expiry is given as days/hours/minutes (omitted components count as 0; total must be between 1 minute and 28 days). When utm_parameters.enabled is true, source/medium/campaign must be non-empty after the merge. Provide at least one group. Returns the updated settings.

enabled.description: Whether UTM parameters are appended to campaign URLs. Default stays as-is.

utm_parameters.description: UTM defaults appended to campaign URLs. Provide only the fields you want to change.

fallback_notification.description: Notification shown if the browser cannot fetch the sent notification. Title, message, and URL are all required by the API, so any you omit are kept from the current values.

fallback_attributes.description: Fallback subscriber city/country used when the browser can't resolve them.

default_expiry.description: Default notification expiry. Set as days/hours/minutes; omitted components count as 0. Total must be between 1 minute and 28 days.

tools.name: pushengage_update_campaign_defaults
tools.title: Update campaign defaults

tools.description: Returns the current site's Service Worker Settings (from the Advanced Settings page), using the dashboard labels: enable_service_worker_registration ("Enable the service worker registration from PushEngage"), enable_service_worker_in_subfolder ("Enable addition of service worker in another sub-folder"), and service_worker_file_path ("Path for service worker file").
tools.name: pushengage_get_service_worker_settings
tools.title: Get service worker settings

tools.description: Updates the current site's Service Worker Settings. Pass only the fields you want to change: enable_service_worker_registration, enable_service_worker_in_subfolder, and/or service_worker_file_path. The tool reads the current values and merges your changes. When enable_service_worker_registration is true, service_worker_file_path must be non-empty after the merge. Provide at least one field. Returns the updated settings.

enable_service_worker_registration.description: Enable the service worker registration from PushEngage. Disable it only if your site already registers its own service worker. When true, service_worker_file_path is required.

enable_service_worker_in_subfolder.description: Enable addition of service worker in another sub-folder.

service_worker_file_path.description: Path for service worker file. Required when the service worker registration is enabled.

tools.name: pushengage_update_service_worker_settings
tools.title: Update service worker settings

tools.description: Lists segments on the current site, paginated (response includes `has_more`). Each item carries segment_id, name, current subscriber count, status, and any URL matching criteria.

limit.description: How many segments to return in this page. Min 1, max 100, default 10. To browse past the first 100, increase `page` instead of asking for a larger limit.

page.description: Page number (1-indexed) for paginating beyond the first batch. e.g. with limit=100 the second page (segments 101–200) is page=2.

name_contains.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter on segment_name.

tools.name: pushengage_list_segments
tools.title: List segments

tools.description: Creates a new segment on the current site. Required: segment_name. Optionally pass segment_criteria with URL `include` and/or `exclude` rules to define what subscribers belong to the segment — each rule is `{ rule: "start" | "exact" | "contains", value: "<url>" }`. By default, segment criteria are evaluated only when a visitor subscribes to push notifications. Set add_segment_on_page_load=true (Segment on Page Visit) to evaluate those criteria on every page visit instead, so segment membership can change as subscribers browse the site. Only include segment_criteria and add_segment_on_page_load when the user explicitly describes the matching rules.

rule.description: How the URL match is evaluated: "start" — the subscriber's page URL starts with `value`; "exact" — the URL exactly equals `value`; "contains" — the URL contains `value`.

value.description: The URL or URL fragment to match against, per the chosen rule.

include.description: URL rules whose match adds a subscriber to this segment. May be empty.

exclude.description: URL rules whose match removes (or prevents adding) a subscriber from this segment. May be empty.

segment_criteria.description: URL-based include/exclude rules that decide which subscribers belong to this segment. Omit to create a name-only segment that the user populates later via the dashboard or workflows. When provided, at least one of `include` or `exclude` must have rules.

add_segment_on_page_load.description: Segment on Page Visit. By default (false), segment criteria (such as URL rules) are evaluated only when a visitor subscribes to push notifications. Set to true to evaluate those criteria on every page visit instead, so segment membership can change as subscribers browse your site.

tools.name: pushengage_create_segment
tools.title: Create a segment

tools.description: Lists subscriber attributes (custom keys set on subscribers via the JS SDK) on the current site, paginated (response includes `has_more`). Use this to discover attribute `key` values before constructing an audience-group filter rule with field="attributes".

limit.description: How many attributes to return in this page. Min 1, max 100, default 10. To browse past the first 100, increase `page` instead of asking for a larger limit.

page.description: Page number (1-indexed) for paginating beyond the first batch.

key_contains.description: Optional substring filter on the attribute `key`. Maps to API `key_like`. Use this when looking up an attribute by name (e.g. searching for "plan" to find the "plan" attribute key).

tools.name: pushengage_list_attributes
tools.title: List subscriber attributes

tools.description: Creates a new subscriber attribute on the current site. Required: `name` (human-readable label, e.g. "Customer Plan") and `key` (machine identifier, e.g. "plan"). The `key` must start with a letter and contain only letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores. The created `key` becomes a usable value for audience-group rules with field="attributes" (the rule's `key` property). PushEngage caps each site at 50 attributes; the API returns 422 if the limit is exceeded.

name.description: Human-readable attribute name shown in the dashboard. 1–128 chars. e.g. "Customer Plan", "Sign-up Source".

key.description: The machine identifier used in the JavaScript SDK and in audience-group rules. Must start with a letter and only contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores. Max 64 chars. e.g. "plan", "signup_source", "lifetime-value". This is the same key you pass as `key` on an audience-group rule with field="attributes".

tools.name: pushengage_create_attribute
tools.title: Create a subscriber attribute

tools.description: Lists the location and device values recorded on this site, with how many active subscribers carry each one. These are the values a `subscriber_filter` rule can use for the country, state, city, device and device_type fields — the "Custom Audience" targeting on the send tools and pushengage_create_audience_group. Call this BEFORE writing a rule on any of those five fields. Locations are display names taken from the subscribers themselves, not ISO codes, and they differ per site — "US", "USA" and "United States" are not interchangeable, and a guessed spelling produces a notification that saves successfully and reaches the wrong people. The subscriber counts also show whether a filter is worth sending at all. For the other two filter vocabularies use pushengage_list_segments (segment names) and pushengage_list_attributes (attribute keys).

fields.description: Which filter fields to list values for. Each name is a `field` you can use in a subscriber_filter rule. "country", "state" and "city" are the subscriber locations recorded on this site — display names taken from the subscribers themselves, not ISO codes, and different on every site. "device" (mobile/tablet/desktop) and "device_type" (the browser or app platform) have fixed vocabularies, so for those this reports which values this site actually has subscribers on.

limit.description: How many values to return PER field, ordered by subscriber count descending. Min 1, max 500, default 50. A site can have thousands of cities, so this caps the response; each field reports `total_values` and `truncated` so you can tell when the list was cut short.

value_contains.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter on the value names, applied across every requested field. Use it to check one value ("do I have subscribers in Pune?") instead of pulling the whole list.

tools.name: pushengage_list_audience_filter_values
tools.title: List values for custom-audience filter fields

tools.description: Lists audience groups on the current site, paginated (response includes `has_more`). Use this to look up audience-group IDs when the user references a group by name; those IDs are what pushengage_send_notification / pushengage_send_ab_notification accept in their `audience_groups` field.

limit.description: How many audience groups to return in this page. Min 1, max 100, default 10. To browse past the first 100, increase `page` instead of asking for a larger limit.

page.description: Page number (1-indexed) for paginating beyond the first batch. e.g. with limit=100 the second page (101–200) is page=2.

name_contains.description: Optional substring filter on the audience-group name. Maps to API `name_like`.

tools.name: pushengage_list_audience_groups
tools.title: List audience groups

tools.description: Creates a new audience group on the current site. Required: `name` and `filter`. The `filter` is a subscriber-filter expression — { op: "or" | "and" (default "or"), value: 2-D array of rule groups }. Each rule is { field, op, value?, key? }. Rules WITHIN a group are AND-ed; groups in `value` are combined with the top-level `op`. See the inputSchema field descriptions for the supported `field` and `op` enums. Common patterns: "Mobile subscribers" → filter={ op: "or", value: [[{ field: "device", op: "in", value: ["mobile"] }]] }. "Subscribed in the last 7 days" → filter={ op: "or", value: [[{ field: "ts_created", op: "ts_elapsed_lt", value: 604800 }]] }. "Highly engaged" (≥20 sent AND ≥2 clicks) → filter={ op: "or", value: [[{ field: "sent_count", op: "gt", value: 20 }, { field: "click_count", op: "gt", value: 2 }]] }. "Sports Fans segment on mobile" → filter={ op: "or", value: [[{ field: "segments", op: "in", value: ["Sports Fans"] }, { field: "device", op: "in", value: ["mobile"] }]] } — segment NAMES are resolved to ids automatically. Call pushengage_list_audience_filter_values before any country/state/city/device/device_type rule and pushengage_list_attributes before any attributes rule: those values are site-specific, and a guessed one saves successfully but matches nobody. Only set description and complex filters when the user explicitly describes them.

description.description: Optional human-readable description, up to 256 chars.

op.description: How groups in `value` combine: "or" (default) means a subscriber matches if ANY group matches; "and" means EVERY group must match. Rules WITHIN a group are always AND-ed.

field.description: Which subscriber property to match. Each field accepts only certain operators — see `op`.

op.description: Comparison operator. Allowed values depend on `field`: country/state/city/device/device_type → in, nin. segments → in (any of), all (all of), nin (none of). sent_count/view_count/click_count → eq, lt, gt, lte, gte. ts_created/ts_last_sent/ts_last_view/ts_last_click → lt (before), gt (after), ts_elapsed_lt (in the last N seconds), ts_elapsed_gt (older than N seconds). profile_id/device_token_hash → in. attributes → any operator, including exists / not_exists.

value.description: The match value. Omit entirely for exists / not_exists. Array for in / nin / all. Positive integer seconds for ts_elapsed_gt / ts_elapsed_lt. For segments, pass segment NAMES as strings (resolved automatically) or numeric segment IDs.

key.description: Required ONLY when field="attributes" — the attribute key to look up. Call pushengage_list_attributes to discover valid keys. Must be omitted for every other field.

value.description: 2-D array: outer is a list of rule-groups (max 15), each inner group is an AND-ed list of rules (1–50). With the default op="or", a subscriber matches if any group's rules all match.

filter.description: Required. The subscriber-filter expression that decides which subscribers belong to this group. Use SubscriberFilterSchema: an outer op ("or"/"and") + a 2-D `value` array (groups of AND-ed rules). Each rule is { field, op, value?, key? }. Example — "all mobile subscribers": { op: "or", value: [[{ field: "device", op: "in", value: ["mobile"] }]] }. Example — "subscribed in the last 7 days": { op: "or", value: [[{ field: "ts_created", op: "ts_elapsed_lt", value: 604800 }]] }. (604800 = 7 × 24 × 3600 seconds.)

tools.name: pushengage_create_audience_group
tools.title: Create an audience group

tools.description: Lists push notifications on the current site, newest first, paginated (response includes `has_more`). Use this to discover notification IDs and review past or upcoming sends. Set include_analytics=true only when the user asks for stats — it costs an extra lookup and adds rolled-up counts and goal conversions to each row. Each item carries content, status, targeting criteria, and delivery stats; the criteria.audience_groups ids are reusable as the send tools' audience_groups input, and absent criteria means the notification went to all subscribers.

limit.description: How many notifications to return in this page. Min 1, max 100, default 10. To browse past the first 100, increase `page` instead of asking for a larger limit.

page.description: Page number (1-indexed) for paginating beyond the first batch.

status.description: Filter by status, matching the dashboard tabs: "sent" (includes currently sending), "scheduled" (includes active and paused recurring notifications), "draft" (includes archived). "all" (default) returns every status.

sent_after.description: Only notifications sent on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD, site timezone). Must be 2017-07-01 or later, and must be paired with sent_before.

sent_before.description: Only notifications sent on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD, site timezone). Must be paired with sent_after and be on or after it.

tags.description: Only notifications carrying at least one of these tags (up to 5).

exclude_tags.description: Exclude notifications carrying any of these tags (up to 5).

include_analytics.description: When true, merge in full delivery analytics (A/B variant totals and subscriber-timezone child sends roll up into the parent row) and goal conversions (goal_count/goal_value per row). Costs extra lookups; only set it when the user asks for stats/performance.

tools.name: pushengage_list_notifications
tools.title: List notifications

tools.description: Creates and sends a push notification on the current site. Required fields: title, message, url. Do not add optional fields (tags, image_url, utm_params, audience_groups, actions, etc.) unless the user explicitly asks for them — for example, do not infer tags from the notification topic. Delivery modes (mutually exclusive — pick AT MOST one): (a) status="schedule" + schedule_date for a one-shot scheduled send; (b) pass recurring_schedule { days, times, start_date, end_date } for a recurring/repeating notification — leave status at "sent" (default) to activate the recurrence, or use "draft" to save without activating; (c) when scheduling one-shot, optionally pass send_in_subscribers_timezone=true to deliver at the scheduled wall-clock time in each subscriber's local timezone (only when the user explicitly asks, e.g. "send at 9am in their timezone"). Otherwise the notification is sent immediately. Use status="draft" to save without sending or activating. Audience — the three options the dashboard offers, pick AT MOST one (they are mutually exclusive): omit both fields for "Send to All Subscribers"; pass `audience_groups` (1-20 predefined audience-group IDs) for "Send to Audience Group" when the user names a saved group; or pass `subscriber_filter` for "Send to Custom Audience" — targeting by segment, attribute, location, device, browser, subscription or engagement date, or sent/view/click counts. Segment names in subscriber_filter are resolved automatically, so "send to my Sports Fans segment" needs no lookup — but call pushengage_list_audience_filter_values first for any country/state/city/device/device_type value, and pushengage_list_attributes first for any attribute `key`, because those are site-specific and a guessed value produces a notification that saves successfully and reaches the wrong people. When the user asks to use the site URL, call pushengage_list_sites and use the current site's site_url.

url.description: Destination URL when the subscriber clicks the notification

status.description: Send now (sent), schedule for later (schedule), or save without sending (draft)

schedule_date.description: Required when status is "schedule". Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss in the site timezone.

image_url.description: Small notification icon. Only when the user explicitly asks for an image.

big_image_url.description: Large hero image. Only when the user explicitly asks for a big image.

expire_in.description: Expiry in seconds (60–2419200). Only when the user explicitly asks.

tags.description: Up to 5 tags, 36 chars each. Only when the user explicitly asks for tags.

actions.description: Action buttons. Only when the user explicitly asks.

utm_params.description: UTM tracking params. Only when the user explicitly asks.

audience_groups.description: Send to one or more predefined audience groups (1-20 group IDs). Each ID refers to an audience group already configured in PushEngage. Omit this field to send to all subscribers. Only set this when the user mentions a saved/predefined audience group. Mutually exclusive with subscriber_filter.

op.description: How groups in `value` combine: "or" (default) means a subscriber matches if ANY group matches; "and" means EVERY group must match. Rules WITHIN a group are always AND-ed.

field.description: Which subscriber property to match. Each field accepts only certain operators — see `op`.

op.description: Comparison operator. Allowed values depend on `field`: country/state/city/device/device_type → in, nin. segments → in (any of), all (all of), nin (none of). sent_count/view_count/click_count → eq, lt, gt, lte, gte. ts_created/ts_last_sent/ts_last_view/ts_last_click → lt (before), gt (after), ts_elapsed_lt (in the last N seconds), ts_elapsed_gt (older than N seconds). profile_id/device_token_hash → in. attributes → any operator, including exists / not_exists.

value.description: The match value. Omit entirely for exists / not_exists. Array for in / nin / all. Positive integer seconds for ts_elapsed_gt / ts_elapsed_lt. For segments, pass segment NAMES as strings (resolved automatically) or numeric segment IDs.

key.description: Required ONLY when field="attributes" — the attribute key to look up. Call pushengage_list_attributes to discover valid keys. Must be omitted for every other field.

value.description: 2-D array: outer is a list of rule-groups (max 15), each inner group is an AND-ed list of rules (1–50). With the default op="or", a subscriber matches if any group's rules all match.

subscriber_filter.description: OPTIONAL. The dashboard's "Send to Custom Audience": personalize who receives this notification based on segments, location, device and more. Mutually exclusive with audience_groups; omit both for "Send to All Subscribers". A 2-D expression: `value` is a list of rule-groups, rules inside a group are AND-ed, and the top-level `op` combines the groups ("or" by default). Segment rules accept segment NAMES and are resolved automatically, so { field: "segments", op: "in", value: ["Sports Fans"] } works without a lookup. For country, state, city, device or device_type values call pushengage_list_audience_filter_values first; for an attributes rule's `key` call pushengage_list_attributes first. Both are site-specific, and a guessed value saves successfully but reaches the wrong people. Every segment reference and attribute key is verified before anything is sent; an unresolvable one fails the call rather than silently changing who receives the push. Example — mobile subscribers in the Sports Fans segment: { op: "or", value: [[{ field: "segments", op: "in", value: ["Sports Fans"] }, { field: "device", op: "in", value: ["mobile"] }]] }. Example — subscribed in the last 7 days on a paid plan: { op: "or", value: [[{ field: "ts_created", op: "ts_elapsed_lt", value: 604800 }, { field: "attributes", key: "plan", op: "ne", value: "free" }]] }.

android_push.description: Android-specific options. Requires channel_id when set. Only when the user explicitly asks.

ios_push.description: iOS-specific options. Only when the user explicitly asks.

send_in_subscribers_timezone.description: Only valid when status="schedule" (and not combined with recurring_schedule). When true, schedule_date is interpreted in each subscriber's local timezone instead of the site timezone — one delivery is scheduled per subscriber timezone so every recipient receives the push at the same wall-clock time. Only set this when the user explicitly asks for subscriber-timezone delivery (for example: "send at 9am in their timezone").

days.description: Days of the week to send on. Values are lowercase day names. At least one day required.

times.description: Times of day to send (24-hour). HH:mm or HH:mm:ss accepted. e.g. ["09:00", "17:30"]. At least one, up to 100.

start_date.description: First date the recurrence is active. Format: YYYY-MM-DD (site timezone).

end_date.description: Last date the recurrence is active. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Must be on or after start_date.

recurring_schedule.description: OPTIONAL. Turns this into a recurring notification that fires on the chosen days/times between start_date and end_date. Mutually exclusive with status="schedule", schedule_date, and send_in_subscribers_timezone. With recurring_schedule set, leave status at "sent" (default) to activate the recurrence, or use "draft" to save without activating. Only set this when the user explicitly asks for a recurring/repeating notification.

tools.name: pushengage_send_notification
tools.title: Send a push notification

tools.description: Creates an A/B notification on the current site with two variants (variant_a and variant_b). Required: variant_a (title, message, url) and variant_b (title, message, url). By default (intelligent_ab_test omitted) both variants ship as-is to the audience — no automatic winner picking. Pass intelligent_ab_test to enable intelligent / auto-winner mode: each variant is sent to sent_limit_percentage% of subscribers, and after winner_delay_minutes the higher-CTR variant is automatically delivered to the remaining audience (up to sent_limit total). Only include intelligent_ab_test when the user explicitly asks for an intelligent / auto-winner test. Do not add other optional fields (tags, audience_groups, per-variant image_url, utm_params, actions, etc.) unless the user explicitly asks. Audience (pick AT MOST one — mutually exclusive; omit both to send to all subscribers): `audience_groups` (1-20 predefined audience-group IDs), or `subscriber_filter` for "Send to Custom Audience". Both apply to both variants, and subscriber_filter behaves exactly as it does on pushengage_send_notification. Use status="schedule" with schedule_date to schedule for later, or status="draft" to save without sending.

url.description: Destination URL when the subscriber clicks the variant

image_url.description: Small icon for this variant. Only when the user explicitly asks.

big_image_url.description: Large hero image for this variant. Only when the user explicitly asks.

utm_params.description: UTM tracking params for this variant.

status.description: Send now (sent), schedule for later (schedule), or save without sending (draft). The API only accepts sent and scheduled in the body; draft is conveyed via the action query param while the body still carries status="sent".

schedule_date.description: Required when status is "schedule". Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss in the site timezone.

audience_groups.description: Send to one or more predefined audience groups (1-20 group IDs). Applies to both variants. Omit to send to all subscribers. Only set when the user mentions a saved/predefined audience group. Mutually exclusive with subscriber_filter.

op.description: How groups in `value` combine: "or" (default) means a subscriber matches if ANY group matches; "and" means EVERY group must match. Rules WITHIN a group are always AND-ed.

field.description: Which subscriber property to match. Each field accepts only certain operators — see `op`.

op.description: Comparison operator. Allowed values depend on `field`: country/state/city/device/device_type → in, nin. segments → in (any of), all (all of), nin (none of). sent_count/view_count/click_count → eq, lt, gt, lte, gte. ts_created/ts_last_sent/ts_last_view/ts_last_click → lt (before), gt (after), ts_elapsed_lt (in the last N seconds), ts_elapsed_gt (older than N seconds). profile_id/device_token_hash → in. attributes → any operator, including exists / not_exists.

value.description: The match value. Omit entirely for exists / not_exists. Array for in / nin / all. Positive integer seconds for ts_elapsed_gt / ts_elapsed_lt. For segments, pass segment NAMES as strings (resolved automatically) or numeric segment IDs.

key.description: Required ONLY when field="attributes" — the attribute key to look up. Call pushengage_list_attributes to discover valid keys. Must be omitted for every other field.

value.description: 2-D array: outer is a list of rule-groups (max 15), each inner group is an AND-ed list of rules (1–50). With the default op="or", a subscriber matches if any group's rules all match.

subscriber_filter.description: OPTIONAL. "Send to Custom Audience" applied to BOTH variants — same shape and same name-resolution behaviour as pushengage_send_notification's subscriber_filter: segment names resolve to ids, and segment and attribute references are verified before anything is sent. Mutually exclusive with audience_groups; omit both to send to all subscribers.

tags.description: Up to 5 tags, 36 chars each. Only when the user explicitly asks for tags.

sent_limit.description: Total subscriber cap across the test and the winner roll-out. e.g. 10000 means up to 10000 subscribers will be touched in total.

sent_limit_percentage.description: Percentage of sent_limit allocated to each variant for the test phase. e.g. 10 means 10% to A, 10% to B, and the remaining 80% goes to the winner after winner_delay_minutes.

winner_delay_minutes.description: How long to wait (in minutes, max 10080 = 7 days) before picking the winner (higher CTR) and rolling out to the remaining audience.

result_name.description: Optional human-readable label for the A/B test result row.

intelligent_ab_test.description: OPTIONAL. Enables intelligent A/B testing: each variant is delivered to sent_limit_percentage% of subscribers, then after winner_delay_minutes the variant with the higher click-through rate is automatically sent to the remaining audience (up to sent_limit subscribers total). Omit this field to send a plain A/B where both variants ship as-is to the audience with no automatic winner selection. Only include when the user explicitly asks for an intelligent / auto-winner A/B test.

tools.description: Returns a time series of the current site's analytics between start_date and end_date, bucketed by group_by. Use this for trends or metrics over a period; for all-time totals use pushengage_get_analytics_summary instead.

group_by.description: How to bucket the series: one point per day, week, or month.
